description:
FILED s487 (Fable, 2026-09-17) during the s486c merge review.  Wanting to splice run/switchx.t (8 rows, all cause #1702) the runner's own way, Fable ran `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 run/switchx.t --bless-fails --bless-shortfall` in the s486c worktree.  Result: `git diff --stat` = perl-suite-fails.tsv 4691 lines (2246 insertions / 2525 deletions over the two files); re/regexp_unicode_prop.t's 568 rows, re/charset.t's 468 and re/pat.t's 379 all removed-and-re-added (re-sorted), the hand-written header replaced by the generator's; row-shortfall.tsv lost every `<file>\t0\t<FIXED note>` row (the zero rows carry the history of WHY a shortfall closed).  Reverted with `git checkout`, the eight switchx rows spliced by hand from the blessed output (saved in the s486c scratch: fails.blessed-switchx.tsv / shortfall.blessed-switchx.tsv).

The standing rule is "a baseline is edited ROW BY ROW, never re-blessed"; the bless flags exist for the audited case (s434's six-file bless was RATIFIED after READING the rows), so this is a usability trap, not a wrong result -- but a whole-file re-sort makes `git diff` useless for the review that the rule requires.  Fix shape: (a) rewrite only the measured files' blocks in place (keep block order, keep the header text verbatim, keep zero-shortfall rows untouched), or (b) refuse the bless flags unless the run measured every file (`--all`) and say why.  Guard: tools/t row that a one-file bless changes only that file's lines.
=== DONE (s488a) ===
Shape (a), as the task asked.  `tools/lib/PCLBaseline.pm` splices a
line-oriented baseline: comment lines verbatim IN PLACE, untouched keys
byte-identical, a measured key's block rewritten AT ITS OLD POSITION with the
rows still there kept where they were, a new key inserted at its sorted
position, and the run's stamp APPENDED to the header instead of replacing it.
`tools/run-perl-suite.pl` (--bless-fails, --bless-shortfall) and
`tools/sweep-diff.pl` (save-shortfall) now pass the set of keys the run
MEASURED, and that set is what licenses a rewrite; the shortfall's hand-placed
zero rows (`t/op/kvhslice.t 0 #1024 FIXED (was 1)`) survive any bless verbatim
and are never invented.  Guard: `tools/t/baseline-splice.t` (19 rows) â a
one-file bless leaves every other byte identical, and its `git diff` is that
file's block only.  `tools/t/audit-instruments.t` green.
Used immediately by #1834's twelve-row splice (commit d4cc28a6).
subject: tools/run-perl-suite.pl `--bless-fails` / `--bless-shortfall` REWRITE THE WHOLE BASELINE even when the run measured ONE file: a `--jobs 1 run/switchx.t --bless-fails --bless-shortfall` produced a 4,691-line diff in perl-suite-fails.tsv (every file's block re-sorted, the hand-written header replaced) and dropped every ZERO-shortfall row of row-shortfall.tsv together with its FIXED note (kvhslice.t, multideref.t, uni/method.t ...) -- the "touching only the files that run measured" promise holds for ROWS, not for the file; make both per-file (rewrite only the measured files' blocks, keep the header and the zero rows), or say so in the runner's help
